proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees a change, because nothing changes. The incident continues to be visible to cartservice's callers named in the brief — checkoutservice and frontend, and through frontend to loadgenerator — all three of which are already alerting. Escalation should go to whoever owns platform-automation, and should also cover the unexplained caller-side quanta: frontend client spans carry ~1 extra 300ms quantum and checkoutservice ~3 [tr_841cf9191f96], which no dispatch has examined and which may mean shaping on those namespaces too. Fixing cartservice alone would not clear those.
proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect should be observed. The thing that would actually end this incident — detaching the platform-automation traffic-shaping container from cart-service's network namespace and removing its eth0 delay=300ms qdisc [tr_4bd19db93d1e] — is not one of the three available actions, and would show up, once someone with that capability does it, as cartservice HGET/HMSET client spans dropping from ~300ms self time back to sub-millisecond in Tempo, cartservice server spans falling from ~301-306ms to a few ms, and the frontend/checkoutservice latency alerts clearing within one or two scrape intervals.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if recreating cartservice's container would in fact drop the injected qdisc with the old network namespace and the shaping is not re-applied — i.e. if a restart_service on cartservice were followed by Redis child spans returning to sub-millisecond and staying there. Two things argue against betting on that: restart_service's precondition asks for evidence pointing at process state rather than at a change, and the evidence points squarely at a change (a container created by platform-automation three minutes before onset [tr_4bd19db93d1e]) while cartservice's own process is demonstrably healthy and non-restarting [tr_eaff6c089824]; and the shaping has been attached at least four times against one recorded removal over the window [tr_4bd19db93d1e], so any namespace-clearing effect is likely to be undone by the next automation pass. It is also wrong if change history holds a prior cartservice configuration that differs materially from the running one — but the executor has already reported the opposite, that cartservice matches its declared definition in every field, which is exactly what one expects when the injected delay lives in a sibling container rather than in cartservice's config.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is elapsed time: user-visible checkout and cart latency stays at one to three added 300ms quanta per request [tr_841cf9191f96] until a human with namespace-level access intervenes. The risk of the alternatives is worse and is why I am not proposing them. revert_config was already refused with nothing to revert. rollback_image would recreate cartservice at a tag it already runs — the two image updates both land on v1.2.1-cartservice-hotfix.2 [tr_4bd19db93d1e] — so it would reset connections for no diagnostic gain. restart_service is irreversible, would drop in-process cart cache, and if the shaping re-attaches it buys a brief recovery that masks the real cause and burns the cleanest remaining signal.
